label: UGC NET June 2026 Paper 2 — Design of Experiments questions not in the 1–50 set (booklet numbers not known; identified by official question ID)

items.stem: In a plasma etching experiment for testing four levels of radio frequency (RF) power, the one-way ANOVA table is obtained as follows: RF Power — sum of squares 66870.00, df 3; Error — 5344.00, df 16; Total — 72214.00, df 19. The calculated value of the F-ratio will be:
items.explanation: Idea: the F-ratio is the treatment mean square divided by the error mean square, where each mean square is a sum of squares divided by its degrees of freedom. Working: F = (66870/3)/(5344/16) = 22290/334 = 66.7365. Source note: The column heading is printed as 'Sum of sequences'; it means sum of squares. Official answer: C (66.7365).

items.stem: In a randomized block design with four treatments and six blocks, if the sum of squares due to treatments is 177, the sum of squares due to blocks is 195 and the total sum of squares is 477, then the mean sum of squares due to error will be:
items.explanation: Idea: in an RBD the total sum of squares splits into treatments + blocks + error, and the error degrees of freedom are (t − 1)(b − 1). The mean square is the sum of squares divided by its degrees of freedom. Working: SSE = 477 − 177 − 195 = 105; error df = (4−1)(6−1) = 15; MSE = 105/15 = 7. Official answer: A (7).

items.stem: If N is the incidence matrix of a BIBD (v, r, b, k, λ), then the value of |NN′| is:
items.explanation: Idea: for a BIBD, NN′ has r on the diagonal and λ everywhere else. That matrix has one eigenvalue rk and v − 1 eigenvalues equal to r − λ, and the determinant is their product. Working: NN′ = (r − λ)I + λJ, whose eigenvalues are r + (v−1)λ = rk (once) and r − λ (v − 1 times), so |NN′| = rk(r − λ)^(v−1). Official answer: B (rk(r − λ)^(v−1)).

items.stem: A 2³ factorial experiment with the factors A, B and C is replicated twice. The error degrees of freedom will be:
items.explanation: Idea: count degrees of freedom. 2³ × 2 = 16 observations give 15 total df; the 7 treatment combinations beyond the first give 7 df; the rest is error (one fewer if the replicates are blocks). Working: 16 runs: total df 15, treatment (7 factorial effects) df 7, so error df = 15 − 7 = 8 when the replicates are completely randomized. Source note: If the two replicates are laid out as blocks (RBD), one more df goes to blocks and error df = 15 − 7 − 1 = 7 (option 2). The official key (8) assumes completely randomized replication. Official answer: A (8).

items.stem: Which of the following designs use all the three principles of design of experiments? A. Completely Randomized Design (CRD) B. Randomized Block Design (RBD) C. Latin Square Design (LSD) D. Balanced Incomplete Block Design (BIBD) Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Idea: the three principles are randomization, replication and local control (blocking). CRD has no blocking; RBD blocks in one direction and the Latin square in two. Working: Randomization, replication and local control: CRD has no local control; RBD (one blocking factor) and LSD (two) use all three. Source note: A BIBD also uses blocking, randomization and replication; the official key (B and C only) follows the usual textbook list of the three basic designs. Official answer: C (B and C only).
